title: QuEst parameter catalog
description: Canonical descriptions for parameters exposed by the command line workflows, default settings, and web UI.

pdb.label: Structure file
pdb.description: Path to the structure file (PDB/CIF), or a bare four-character RCSB PDB ID used for AV calculation.

attachment.chain.label: Attachment chain
attachment.chain.description: Chain identifier of the amino acid residue where the dye is tethered.

attachment.residue.label: Attachment residue
attachment.residue.description: Residue sequence number of the amino acid where the dye is tethered.

attachment.atom.label: Attachment atom
attachment.atom.description: Atom name (e.g., CB, CA) used as the tethering point for the dye.

av_parameter.linker_length.label: Linker length
av_parameter.linker_length.description: Maximum distance from attachment point to the center of the dye.

av_parameter.linker_width.label: Linker width
av_parameter.linker_width.description: Width of the linker tethering the dye.

av_parameter.radius1.label: Dye radius
av_parameter.radius1.description: Exclusion radius representing the dye sphere (single-sphere approximation).

av_parameter.allowed_sphere_radius.label: Allowed sphere
av_parameter.allowed_sphere_radius.description: Radius around the attachment atom inside which the linker ignores obstacles, so it can leave the atom it is tied to. On by default at FPS's 2.25 Å (0.5 × the 4.5 Å linker width); the attachment atom itself is never an obstacle.

av_parameter.radius_scale.label: Obstacle radius scale
av_parameter.radius_scale.description: Factor on the atoms' van der Waals radii (IMP's united-atom set) when they are obstacles to the linker and the dye. The default, 0.84, matches FPS's smaller Bondi radii: at it the T4L CB-site volumes agree with FPS's own routine. 1.0 uses IMP's radii as they are.

dg.label: Grid resolution
dg.description: Grid resolution used to compute the accessible volume (AV) and diffusion search space.

tau0.label: Unquenched lifetime
tau0.description: Fluorescence lifetime of the donor dye in the absence of quenching.

fret.dyes.0.D.label: Donor diffusion coefficient
fret.dyes.0.D.description: Diffusion coefficient of the donor dye in solution, when not interacting with the protein surface.

ensemble.label: Ensemble
ensemble.description: Where the dye sits during the excited state. 'walk': Brownian walkers, each started from the equilibrium occupancy (w = product of slow_factor^-1 over the residues in range), and a photon race along each; the only ensemble that simulates FRET, with Monte-Carlo noise. 'equilibrium': the static limit, every position decays on its own at 1/tau0 + kQ, weighted by w; exact and fast, what the inverse fit uses. 'pde': the diffusion equation on the AV grid with stickiness as a potential and quenching as a sink, solved without sampling noise; it includes motion during the excited state, and its stationary state is the equilibrium ensemble. The walk and the PDE describe the same physics and agree to the walk's time-step bias.

critical_distance.label: Fallback contact radius
critical_distance.description: Contact radius used by residue types that do not define their own quench_radius. It is measured from the dye centre to the residue's quenching centre, so it must exceed the dye radius plus van der Waals contact (typically 7-9 A for a 3.5 A dye).

t_max.label: Simulation time
t_max.description: Simulated time per trajectory block (walk ensemble). The walk covers parallel_trajectories × t_max in all, cut into walkers of 20–50 × tau0 (about 1000 of them) that each start from the equilibrium occupancy. Unused by the equilibrium and PDE ensembles.

t_step.label: Time step
t_step.description: Time step of the Brownian walk (walk ensemble). A smaller step shrinks the walk's bias at sticky boundaries; the equilibrium and PDE ensembles do not step.

n_photons.label: Simulated photons
n_photons.description: Number of excitation photons simulated to reconstruct the fluorescence decay histogram.

n_bins.label: Decay bins
n_bins.description: Number of time channels/bins used to construct the output decay histogram.

parallel_trajectories.label: Parallel trajectories
parallel_trajectories.description: Number of t_max-long trajectory blocks in the walk ensemble. The walkers are vectorised, so this sets the total simulated time, not a thread count. Use -1 for the number of CPU cores, capped at 8.

slow_radius.label: Slowing radius
slow_radius.description: Radius around each whole-protein amino-acid center where that residue type contributes its slow_factor to the diffusion coefficient grid.

save_avs.label: Save AV files
save_avs.description: Whether to save the calculated accessible volume grids as XYZ files.

output_file.label: Output file prefix
output_file.description: Base filename prefix used when saving simulation outputs, trajectories, and decays.

skip_frame.label: Trajectory skip frames
skip_frame.description: Subsampling factor for writing trajectory frames to coordinates files.

fret.enabled.label: FRET enabled
fret.enabled.description: Whether a FRET acceptor dye is simulated to compute FRET efficiency and decay curves.

fret.R0_matrix.label: Förster radius
fret.R0_matrix.description: Förster radius R0 of the donor–acceptor pair, in Ångström like every other length in a project. Stored as the donor→acceptor cell of fret.R0_matrix; the transfer rate scales as (R0/r)^6, so entering nanometres makes FRET vanish. Typical xanthene pairs are 45–65 Å.

fret.kappa2.label: Orientation factor κ²
fret.kappa2.description: Orientation factor κ² of the transfer, between 0 (perpendicular transition dipoles) and 4 (collinear). QuEst does not model it: the dye is a point diffusing in a volume and has no dipole to orient, so this is the averaging regime you are asserting. The default 2/3 is the isotropic dynamic average, which is what a published Förster radius already assumes — leaving it there reproduces the rate exactly. Raise it only with evidence that both dyes are orientationally restricted.

fret.dyes.1.attachment.chain.label: Acceptor chain
fret.dyes.1.attachment.chain.description: Chain identifier of the residue where the FRET acceptor dye is attached.

fret.dyes.1.attachment.residue.label: Acceptor residue
fret.dyes.1.attachment.residue.description: Residue sequence number where the FRET acceptor dye is attached.

fret.dyes.1.attachment.atom.label: Acceptor atom
fret.dyes.1.attachment.atom.description: Atom name where the FRET acceptor dye is attached.

fret.dyes.1.av_parameter.linker_length.label: Acceptor linker length
fret.dyes.1.av_parameter.linker_length.description: Maximum distance from attachment point to the center of the FRET acceptor dye.

fret.dyes.1.av_parameter.linker_width.label: Acceptor linker width
fret.dyes.1.av_parameter.linker_width.description: Width of the linker tethering the FRET acceptor dye.

fret.dyes.1.av_parameter.radius1.label: Acceptor dye radius
fret.dyes.1.av_parameter.radius1.description: Exclusion radius representing the FRET acceptor dye sphere.

fret.dyes.1.D.label: Acceptor diffusion coefficient
fret.dyes.1.D.description: Diffusion coefficient of the FRET acceptor dye when not interacting with the protein surface.

amino_acid_interactions.label: Amino-acid interactions
amino_acid_interactions.description: Per-residue-type interaction table. Each entry holds slow_factor (0-1, how much the residue slows the diffusing dye), kQ (quenching rate in 1/ns applied on contact), quench_radius (contact radius in Angstrom from the dye centre; null inherits critical_distance) and quench_atoms (atom names whose centroid defines the quenching centre). Only residues with a redox-active side chain quench by default: TRP, TYR, MET, HIS, CYS and PRO.

amino_acid_interactions.kQ.label: Quenching rate kQ
amino_acid_interactions.kQ.description: Rate at which this residue type quenches the dye while the two are in contact. Contributions from residues whose contact spheres overlap add up.

amino_acid_interactions.quench_radius.label: Contact radius
amino_acid_interactions.quench_radius.description: Distance from the dye centre to this residue's quenching centre within which quenching occurs. Leave empty to inherit the project-wide critical_distance.

amino_acid_interactions.quench_atoms.label: Quenching centre atoms
amino_acid_interactions.quench_atoms.description: Atom names whose centroid defines this residue's quenching centre. The defaults follow the redox-active moiety that mediates photo-induced electron transfer: the indole ring for TRP, the phenol ring for TYR, the imidazole ring for HIS, SD for MET and SG for CYS - not CB.

amino_acid_interactions.slow_factor.label: Slow factor
amino_acid_interactions.slow_factor.description: Factor between 0 and 1 scaling the dye's diffusion coefficient near this residue type, modelling unspecific stickiness. Overlapping residues multiply their factors.

coarse_grained.label: Coarse-grained structure
coarse_grained.description: Reduce the structure to backbone plus CB before simulating, with CB moved to the side-chain centre of mass. Side-chain atoms are then absent, so every residue's quenching centre falls back to that CB pseudo-atom, and the accessible volume grows because side chains no longer block it. This is a modelling choice, not a speed optimisation: QuEst's cost is dominated by the AV grid rather than the atom count.

random_seed.label: Random seed
random_seed.description: Seed for the Monte-Carlo simulation. When set, both the diffusion trajectory and the photon trace are seeded, so repeated runs of the same project reproduce the same decay and quantum yield exactly. Leave unset for an independent random run; the photon trace then uses a faster multi-threaded kernel.

fret.acceptor_dynamics.label: Acceptor dynamics
fret.acceptor_dynamics.description: How the acceptor is treated: 'trajectory' simulates its Brownian walk with its own diffusion coefficient and stickiness and uses the instantaneous donor-acceptor distance, 'averaged' averages over its static accessible volume (the fast-acceptor limit, valid only when it explores that volume quickly compared with the donor lifetime). The two disagree because a cloud is weighted uniformly while a trajectory is weighted by where the dye dwells.

fret.dyes.1.slow_radius.label: Acceptor slowing radius
fret.dyes.1.slow_radius.description: Radius around each amino-acid centre within which that residue slows the acceptor. Separate from the donor's: a cyanine and a rhodamine do not adhere to a protein surface in the same way. Defaults to the donor's value.

fret.dyes.1.amino_acid_interactions.label: Acceptor interactions
fret.dyes.1.amino_acid_interactions.description: Per-residue-type interaction table for the acceptor, same shape as the donor's amino_acid_interactions. Only slow_factor is used, since QuEst reports the donor's decay and the acceptor's own PET quenching would change how bright the acceptor is, not the donor. Defaults to the donor's table.
